properties.role: Tide-reader who rows boats out of Gullwick Docks
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her; never looks anyone in the eye, keeps her gaze on the tide line; curt, keeps mending her net.
properties.wants: Will row the party to the chapel, but never at night.
properties.knows: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang, forty years ago; her grandmother said the water came up warm. Hers is the only boat that goes near the bell water.

sources.quote: She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: New named NPC the GM voiced; the GM confirmed both spellings of her name.

sources.quote: There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net.

changes.why: She works the docks.

sources.quote: She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Where the table last saw her.

properties.details_shown: Fog, tar, and gulls; the far piers are rotting. Morning fog sits on the docks; pier four is where boats can be found, with an upturned skiff on the planks.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.

changes.why: The GM described pier four.

change.name: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang

properties.statement: Forty years ago the Saltmere Mine flooded the same night the bell first rang, and the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Sela links the mine's closing to the bell; the warm water is her grandmother's account.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang.

changes.why: The fact is about the mine.

sources.quote: My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Sela is the source.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. The entrance is a black mouth in the chalk with a half-rotted timber frame and a rusted cart on its side. Warm air smells of church, of old candle wax. About thirty paces in the tunnel is flooded with warm black water, with wet hymn-book pages floating on it and stuck to the walls.
properties.state: Closed; the tunnel is flooded with warm water about thirty paces in.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side. The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch.

changes.why: The party saw the mine; the GM described it.

change.name: Hymn-book pages in the Saltmere tunnel, one marked M. Brand

properties.statement: Wet hymn-book pages float in the flooded Saltmere tunnel. One carries a hymn about the sea giving back what it takes, with "M. Brand" in pencil in the margin.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: A clue the GM placed; whose hand wrote it is only Teo's claim.

sources.quote: Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: Found in the mine.

properties.what_changed: Mira heard the bell the night she left. In the Saltmere Mine, a hymn page marked "M. Brand" turned up, and Teo recognises it as Mira's handwriting and believes she was there.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Teo ties the clue to his goal; the handwriting is his claim.

change.name: Is Maren Vosk in the cult?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa and Oren suspect the harbor-master Maren of being behind the bell and running the choir. Only the players' theory so far.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

changes.why: Player theory, recorded as a thread only.

sources.quote: Maren wanted us gone from day one.

changes.why: The theory is about Maren.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof sticks out of the bay: just the bell tower and two broken arches, with seaweed hanging from the stones.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.

changes.why: The GM described the chapel.

properties.statement: Fishermen say the Kelp Mother pulls children who stand too close to the water down by the ankles.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say.

changes.why: Local legend only; the GM did not confirm it is real.

change.name: Pale congregation under the water at midnight

properties.statement: At midnight, as the bell rang twelve times and a louder humming rose, pale shapes stood in rows on the chapel floor under the water like a congregation, then vanished when the bell stopped.

sources.quote: And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: First sight of the drowned congregation.

sources.quote: Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows.

changes.why: They stand in the chapel.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.
And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago.

changes.why: The bell rang again and the GM states the clock stands at three of six.

properties.details_shown: A tavern by the docks. A fire going, and it smells of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

changes.why: New location where the party stays.

properties.played_as: Huge, red-bearded, laughs at his own jokes, wipes the same mug the whole time he talks. Teasing and generous toward the party.
properties.knows: Has known Maren for thirty years: sharp tongue, good heart.

sources.quote: Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.
Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: New named NPC the GM voiced.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: He runs the inn.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: Where the table last saw him.

change.name: Maren lost a brother to the bay

properties.statement: Maren Vosk lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Bram's account of Maren's past.

sources.quote: She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: The fact is about Maren.

properties.what_is_open: The party wants to reach the drowned chapel, where Teo thinks the hymns came from. Mira wrote in the hymn book.
properties.next_step: Meet Sela at pier four at first light, be rowed out, and dive to the chapel at low tide by day. Vessa buys rope and a second lantern tonight.

sources.quote: Okay, plan. Mira wrote in that hymn book. The chapel is where the hymns came from. We go down to the chapel.
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: The party's plan for the next session.

sources.quote: we dive to the chapel at low tide

changes.why: Destination.

sources.quote: Sela rows us out

changes.why: She is the boatwoman.
